patients.summary: Insulin-treated type 2 diabetic with CKD 3b, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and a 40 pack-year smoking habit who joined in March 2025. That July a hotel-acquired Legionella pneumonia needed ICU care and was complicated on hospital day 10 by line-associated Candida albicans candidemia; he recovered, was last seen at his October physical, and in January 2026 had an outside admission for right lower lobe pneumonia that the practice knows only from records.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

Reason: transferring care. His previous office is relocating.

HPI: 62 y/o man, regional sales manager, here to set up primary care. Type 2 diabetes since roughly 2012, on insulin since 2018: glargine 24 units at bedtime plus lispro on a correction scale with meals. Checks sugars before meals most days; says fasting numbers usually sit a little above where he'd like. No lows that needed help from anyone. Was told a few years ago his kidney function is in the stage 3b range; his old office tracked it with blood work. BP treated with lisinopril and amlodipine, no home cuff. Takes atorvastatin and a baby aspirin. He travels much of the month for work, lots of restaurant meals and hotel stays.

PMH: T2DM on insulin; CKD 3b; HTN since about 2010; hyperlipidemia.
PSH: laparoscopic cholecystectomy, 2010.
Meds: insulin glargine 24 u qHS; insulin lispro sliding scale with meals; lisinopril 10 daily; amlodipine 5 daily; atorvastatin 40 daily; aspirin 81 daily.
Allergies: none known to medications.
Family: father had T2DM with kidney involvement and died of a heart attack at 68. Mother with HTN and CKD stage 3. Older brother has coronary disease.
Social: smokes cigarettes, about 40 pack-years total. Not ready to stop; willing to revisit. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a week. No other substances.

ROS: no chest pain, no dyspnea, no claudication, no visual change, no numbness in the feet, no urinary symptoms. Otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, BP at goal. Well appearing, overweight. Fundi not examined (undilated). Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed laparoscopic scars. No peripheral edema. Feet: skin intact, no calluses or ulcers; monofilament felt at all sites both feet; DP and PT pulses 2+ bilaterally.

Assessment and plan:
1. T2DM on basal-bolus insulin, with CKD. A1c and urine albumin/creatinine today. Same insulin doses for now. Optometry referral for a dilated eye exam.
2. CKD stage 3b. CMP today. Stays on lisinopril. Avoid NSAIDs; he uses acetaminophen when needed.
3. HTN, controlled on lisinopril and amlodipine. Continue.
4. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40. Lipid panel today.
5. Tobacco. Advised to quit; he declines a medication or a quit date today. Qualifies for lung cancer screening; low-dose CT ordered after discussing false positives and follow-up scans.
6. Health maintenance: PCV20 and Shingrix #1 given today, second Shingrix in 2-6 months. Hep C and HIV screening sent. Colonoscopy reportedly done in 2021; will confirm from records. PHQ-2 negative.

Return 3 months, sooner by message or phone.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wayne, your labs from yesterday are back. A1c is 7.8, a bit above our target of around 7, so there is room to tighten things up; let's look at your meter readings together in June before changing insulin. Kidney function is in the same stage 3b range your old office described, and no protein is leaking into the urine, which is good news. Cholesterol is well controlled on atorvastatin. Blood counts are normal and the hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Received 41 pages from the patient's previous primary care office (covering 2016-2025).

Problem list: type 2 diabetes, insulin requiring; chronic kidney disease stage 3b; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; tobacco use.
Medication list matches what he reported at his new patient visit.
Surgical: laparoscopic cholecystectomy 2010.
Screening: screening colonoscopy 2021, normal exam, no polyps; repeat advised in 10 years.
Immunizations: Tdap 2019.
No drug allergies recorded.

PCP reviewed; nothing that changes current plan. Colonoscopy marked done in health maintenance.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
Indication: lung cancer screening, current smoker, 40 pack-years. Baseline exam.
Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
Comparison: none.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or pleural effusion. Central airways patent. Heart size normal, no pericardial effusion. No enlarged mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes. Visualized upper abdomen notable only for surgical absence of the gallbladder. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung screening CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your screening CT came back clean: no nodules or spots, which radiology scores as Lung-RADS 1. The plan is to repeat it every spring while you're still smoking or within 15 years of quitting. Whenever you're ready to talk about quitting, I'm here for that conversation.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I examined Mr. Alden on 04/29/2025 for his annual diabetic eye evaluation. Corrected acuity good in both eyes. Pupils normal. Pressures within normal range. Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy in either eye, no macular edema, optic nerves healthy.

Impression: diabetes without retinopathy.
Plan: repeat dilated exam in one year. Updated reading prescription given.

Medications per patient: insulin glargine, insulin lispro, lisinopril, amlodipine, atorvastatin, aspirin. Allergies: NKDA.

Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back for diabetes and BP. Brought his meter: fasting values mildly high on travel weeks, better at home. Rare pre-dinner lows when he skips lunch on the road, always caught early with juice. Taking everything as prescribed. Still smoking, has not cut down. No chest pain, no breathing trouble, no foot problems. Eye exam last month showed no retinopathy.

O: Vitals per flowsheet; BP controlled. Lungs clear, heart regular. No ankle swelling. Feet without lesions.
Point-of-care A1c 7.5 (was 7.8 in March).

A/P:
- T2DM with CKD: moving in the right direction. Keep glargine 24 units. Talked about packing a lunch or a snack on long drives to avoid skipping meals with mealtime insulin on board.
- CKD 3b: BMP drawn today.
- HTN: at goal, no changes.
- Tobacco: quitting discussed again, he's not interested in nicotine replacement or pills at this point.
- Shingrix #2 given today, series complete.

Next visit in about 4 months, with fasting labs and a physical in the fall.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER, EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 12:50

Chief complaint: fever and diarrhea, now coughing.

HPI: 62-year-old man with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, CKD 3b, hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Two days ago developed fever, loose watery stools and marked tiredness; since yesterday a dry cough and some breathlessness walking around the house. Got home recently from four nights at a hotel for a sales convention. No sick contacts he knows of.

Home meds: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 10 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Surgical history: lap cholecystectomy.
Social: current smoker, 40 pack-years. Occasional alcohol.
Family history: father with diabetic kidney disease, died of MI at 68; mother HTN and CKD 3; older brother with CAD.

Triage: T 39.1 C (102.4 F), BP 126/76, P 98, SpO2 94% on room air.

Exam: febrile, tired but conversant. Crackles over the right lower lung field. Heart tachycardic-borderline, regular. Abdomen soft, mildly diffusely tender, no guarding. No rash.

Results: Na 126. AST 68, ALT 70. WBC 15.4 with neutrophil predominance (88% neutrophils).
Chest film: patchy right middle and lower lobe infiltrates.
Sputum Gram stain: many segmented neutrophils, no organisms seen.
Urine Legionella antigen: POSITIVE.

MDM: pneumonia with diarrhea, hyponatremia and transaminitis after hotel exposure; urine antigen confirms Legionella. Started IV broad-spectrum coverage plus levofloxacin, renally dosed. Fluid restriction for sodium; insulin continued with hospital correction scale.

Diagnosis: Legionnaires' disease (Legionella pneumonia).
Disposition: admitted to hospital medicine. PCP office notified through the hospital's admission alert. Case reported to the health department per protocol.

events.reason: Legionella pneumonia; course complicated by candidemia

medications.reason: Held for hypotension and acute kidney injury; recheck creatinine after discharge

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily through 08/03/2025

reports.text:
Indication: candidemia, evaluate for endocarditis.
Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness and normal systolic function; estimated LVEF 60%. No regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Aortic, mitral, tricuspid and pulmonic valves structurally normal without vegetation or significant regurgitation. No pericardial effusion. IVC normal with normal respiratory variation.
reports.conclusion: Normal study. No valvular vegetation. LVEF 60%.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Consultation
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
INFECTIOUS DISEASE CONSULT

Reason: yeast in blood cultures.

Blood cultures drawn 07/17 turned positive in under 48 hours in every bottle; identified as Candida albicans. Patient was admitted 07/08 with Legionnaires' disease (urine antigen positive), required an IJ catheter and pressors early, and spiked on day 10.

Recommendations:
1. Start micafungin today.
2. Remove the central venous catheter today. Done at 11:30.
3. Daily blood cultures until negative; therapy runs 14 days from the first negative set.
4. Dilated eye exam by ophthalmology.
5. Transthoracic echo.
6. Once cultures clear, the patient is stable and susceptibilities confirm, step down to oral fluconazole with renal dose adjustment.
7. Levofloxacin for Legionella can finish its 14-day course on 07/21.

Will follow.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Inpatient ophthalmology, requested for candidemia screening.

No visual complaints. Near acuity at baseline each eye. Pupils equal, no APD. Dilated exam: clear vitreous both eyes; no chorioretinal lesions, no white infiltrates, no hemorrhages. No diabetic retinopathy.

Impression: no ocular candidiasis. No ophthalmic follow-up needed for this indication; continue routine diabetic eye care.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 07/08/2025, discharged 07/29/2025.

Principal diagnosis: Legionnaires' disease (Legionella pneumonia), right middle and lower lobes.
Secondary: Candida albicans candidemia, central line associated; acute kidney injury on CKD 3b; hyponatremia, resolved; type 2 diabetes on insulin; hypertension; tobacco use.

Course:
Presented with two days of fever, diarrhea and fatigue followed by cough and dyspnea after a hotel convention stay. Urine Legionella antigen positive. Started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and levofloxacin; narrowed to levofloxacin alone, renally dosed, 14 days completed 07/21. On day 2 became hypotensive; a right IJ central line was placed and he received norepinephrine in the ICU for three days. Transferred to the floor day 6.

On day 10 (07/17) he developed new fever to 38.9 C with tachycardia and hypotension. WBC 14.0, Hgb 10.2, platelets 100, creatinine 2.1 (baseline 1.6). Blood cultures grew Candida albicans in all bottles within 48 hours. ID consulted. Micafungin started 07/19 and the central line removed the same day. Repeat cultures 07/20 and 07/21 no growth. Isolate fluconazole susceptible. Ophthalmology: no eye involvement. TTE: no vegetation, LVEF 60%. Changed to oral fluconazole 07/25.

Lisinopril and amlodipine were held for low pressures and the kidney injury. Amlodipine resumed at discharge now that pressures have recovered. Lisinopril remains on hold.

Discharge labs (07/28): WBC 8.6, Hgb 10.6, platelets 172, sodium 136, creatinine 1.94.

Discharge medications:
- Fluconazole 200 mg by mouth daily through 08/03/2025 (renally adjusted; last dose 08/03)
- Insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime
- Insulin lispro per sliding scale with meals
- Amlodipine 5 mg daily
- Atorvastatin 40 mg daily
- Aspirin 81 mg daily
- HOLD lisinopril until PCP rechecks kidney function

Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within one week with CBC and metabolic panel. Smoking cessation strongly advised; declined nicotine replacement in hospital.
Condition at discharge: stable, ambulating, on room air.

documents.title: Hospital admission alert
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Admission alert from the regional medical center: patient admitted last evening through the ED with pneumonia, urine Legionella antigen positive. PCP aware. Will track the stay and set up follow-up after discharge.

events.reason: New fever, tachycardia and hypotension on hospital day 10

results.text: Candida albicans growing in all bottles (2 of 2 sets). Fluconazole susceptible.

documents.title: Critical Care Evaluation, Hospital Day 10
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
MEDICAL ICU EVALUATION

Asked to see this 62-year-old man, admitted 07/08 with Legionella pneumonia, for a new fever with tachycardia and low blood pressure on hospital day 10. Background: insulin-treated T2DM, CKD 3b, HTN, hyperlipidemia, active smoker. Early in the stay he needed a right internal jugular central line and norepinephrine (days 2-4) in our unit, then was transferred to the floor on day 6 and had been steadily improving on levofloxacin.

This afternoon temperature 38.9 C (102 F), heart rate up and pressures soft.

Home meds (insulin glargine 24 u qHS, lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81): lisinopril and amlodipine on hold in hospital; insulin, statin and aspirin continued. NKDA.
Family and social history as in the admission record.

Exam: warm, alert. Central line site without erythema or drainage. Lungs with a few residual right basilar crackles, unchanged. Abdomen benign. No rash, no joint swelling, no calf tenderness. Nothing new focally to explain the fever.

Labs: WBC 14.0, Hgb 10.2, platelets 100. Creatinine 2.1, up from the 1.6 baseline in our records.

Impression: new sepsis physiology late in the admission without an obvious source, in a diabetic with a central venous catheter and prolonged antibiotic exposure. Line infection, including fungal, high on the list.

Plan: two sets of blood cultures now, one peripheral and one through the line. Fluid bolus, return to the ICU for monitoring. Broaden antibacterial coverage pending cultures. Low threshold to pull the line. Renal dosing for all agents; trend creatinine and platelets.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Transitional care outreach, discharged 7/29.
Spoke with patient. Feels weak and tires on stairs but improving each day. No fever since home, cough much quieter, no shortness of breath at rest. Eating okay. Taking fluconazole once daily, last dose Sunday 8/3. Knows lisinopril is on hold. Sugars running higher than usual since the hospital, no lows.
Med list reconciled against discharge summary.
Visit with PCP Tue 8/5 at 10:30, labs same day. Told to call for fever, chills or worsening breathing.

orders.reason: Follow-up of resolved Legionella pneumonia, smoker over 50

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up (TCM). Discharge summary and ICU/ID notes reviewed.

Interval: three-week admission for Legionella pneumonia caught at a convention hotel, ICU stay with a central line and pressors, then Candida albicans bloodstream infection on day 10 from the line. Line out, cultures cleared, eyes and echo clean. Finished his last fluconazole tablet Sunday.

Today: energy maybe two-thirds of normal, naps in the afternoon. Cough nearly gone, no sputum. No fevers. Bowels normal. Appetite returning; down several kg since spring. Sugars somewhat higher than before; no lows. Still smoking, fewer than before the hospital.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, afebrile, room air sat normal, BP fine on amlodipine alone. Thin-looking compared with March. Right base with no crackles today, lungs clear throughout. Right neck line site healed. No edema. No rash.

Labs today: Hgb 11.5 (10.6 at discharge), creatinine 1.86 (1.94 at discharge; his usual here is high 1s), sodium 139, liver enzymes normal.

A/P:
1. Legionnaires' disease, treated; clinically resolved. Follow-up chest film in about a month to confirm clearing, given his smoking and age.
2. Candidemia, line-related, completed 14 days after clearance. Resolved.
3. AKI on CKD 3b, recovering. Keep lisinopril held for now; repeat BMP in two weeks and restart if creatinine is back near baseline.
4. Anemia of acute illness, improving. Recheck at the fall visit.
5. T2DM: same glargine dose; expect sugars to settle as he recovers. Call if fasting readings stay high or he has lows as he eats less.
6. Tobacco: the hospital stay rattled him and he has cut back; offered patch or varenicline, he wants to try on his own first.

OK to return to desk work next week; no travel for another few weeks.

documents.title: Follow-up labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Wayne, the rest of yesterday's panel looks reassuring: liver tests are back to normal and sodium is normal. Kidney numbers are drifting back toward your usual. Lab slip for the repeat kidney check is in the system for the week of the 18th; no need to fast.

documents.title: Restart lisinopril
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with yesterday's BMP: creatinine 1.80, essentially back to his baseline here; potassium normal. Restarting lisinopril 10 mg daily (he still has tablets at home, new script sent anyway). Will recheck kidney function and potassium at the October physical. He feels close to normal, walking daily. Reminded him the follow-up chest x-ray order is in.

reports.text:
Indication: follow-up after right-sided pneumonia in July.
Comparison: 07/08/2025.
Findings: The previously seen right middle and lower lobe opacities have resolved. Lungs are clear. No effusion or pneumothorax. Heart and mediastinum normal. Surgical clips in the right upper quadrant.
reports.conclusion: Resolution of prior right-sided infiltrates. No acute cardiopulmonary process.

documents.title: RE: x-ray and travel
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the x-ray is clear, thanks. Boss wants me back on the road in October, a two-day trade show and then the usual hotel weeks. Any reason I shouldn't? Kind of nervous about hotels now.

documents.title: RE: x-ray and travel
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Yes, the film shows the pneumonia has fully cleared. You're fine to travel. Legionella outbreaks at hotels are uncommon and usually traced and fixed quickly; there is nothing you need to avoid, though if you ever get fever with cough or diarrhea after a trip, call us the same day and mention the hotel. The single biggest thing that raises your risk for this kind of pneumonia is smoking, so that conversation is still open. See you on the 23rd.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not arrive for 9:30. Reached him by phone: driving back from a client meeting, appointment slipped his mind. Rebooked as his annual physical plus diabetes visit Fri 10/24 at 8:00, fasting labs that morning.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Annual Physical and Diabetes Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM + CHRONIC CARE

Since last seen: lisinopril back on in August without trouble. Follow-up chest film in September clear. Back to traveling this month; went fine. Energy back to normal, walking most evenings at home. Weight has come back partway. Sugars higher in the weeks after the hospital, now settling. No lows. Still smoking; says he is smoking less than before July but not ready to set a quit date.

Current meds: glargine 24 u at bedtime, lispro correction scale with meals, lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81. NKDA.

ROS: negative for chest discomfort, exertional breathlessness, cough, fever, urinary changes, numbness in the feet, visual changes. Mood good; PHQ-2 zero.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Alert, comfortable. HEENT unremarkable. Neck without nodes or thyromegaly. Heart regular rate, no murmurs or gallops. Lungs clear, good air movement. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. No edema. Skin unremarkable. Feet: intact skin, no deformity, monofilament normal bilaterally, pulses palpable. Prostate not examined (PSA by shared decision).

A1c 7.7 today, a little higher than June, as expected after the illness.

Assessment/plan:
- T2DM with CKD: A1c 7.7. Keep glargine 24 u for now; recheck in 3 months and adjust then if it stays above goal. Eye exam due again in spring.
- CKD 3b: CMP and urine albumin/creatinine drawn; on lisinopril.
- HTN: controlled on lisinopril/amlodipine.
- Hyperlipidemia: lipid panel today, atorvastatin 40.
- Post-illness anemia: CBC today.
- Tobacco: counseled again, declines meds. Annual low-dose CT due in April.
- Prostate: discussed PSA screening pros and cons; he wants it checked. Drawn today.
- Vaccines: flu and updated COVID today. Pneumococcal, shingles and Tdap current. Colonoscopy 2021 normal.

Follow-up: diabetes visit in 3 months, around late January. Front desk to book.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wayne, all your physical labs are in. Blood count is back to normal, so the anemia from the hospital has recovered. Kidney function is at your usual stage 3b level with no protein in the urine, and potassium is fine on lisinopril. Cholesterol stays at goal. PSA is normal. A1c was 7.7 as we discussed. Please book the late-January diabetes visit when you have your travel calendar; the front desk can help by text.
